title: Toolchain conduit: prefix reservation, result injection, and safety heuristics for multi-tool streaming
creator: Maya Singh
description: Design and implement a 'toolchain conduit' layer that coordinates multi-tool chaining during streamed responses, enforces safe result injection semantics, and prevents runaway recursion/looping across tool calls while remaining backwards-compatible with older tool schemas.
background: Customer apps increasingly rely on composing multiple tool/function calls inside a single streamed generation (e.g., call a search tool, then a calculator, then an executor). Current runtime supports streaming and tool calling, but lacks a consolidated policy to: 1) reserve prefix slots and KV cache entries for anticipated tool calls, 2) inject tool results into the model context in a way that guarantees schema conformance and deduplication, and 3) detect/mitigate accidental recursion (a tool invoking the runtime which triggers the same tool repeatedly). Past tickets (ENG-27210, ENG-47253, ENG-22177) touch parts but leave gaps in combined streamed multi-tool flows and compatibility for older tool response shapes.
proposed_solution: Introduce a conduit middleware that runs in the serving runtime pipeline. Key pieces: 1) Prefix reservation: allocate ephemeral prefix tokens and KV reservations for tool outputs during the early phase of a streamed response to avoid mid-stream kernel reconfiguration. 2) Result injection policy: canonicalize tool outputs into the structured-output v2 schema before merging into the prompt; include an idempotency marker and a provenance envelope. 3) Recursion/loop guard: maintain a lightweight call-graph snapshot with hop-count and signature hashing; if a signature repeats above a threshold, either rewrite the call to a no-op canned response or escalate via a configured fallback model. 4) Compatibility shim: map legacy tool response keys into the canonical schema at the conduit boundary, with a WARN telemetry event for unmapped fields. 5) Safety heuristics: rate-limit tool calls per request, bound K/V growth, and add configurable student-tolerant backoffs for downstream tools that escalate latency. The conduit should expose toggles via the console (on/off, thresholds) and a compatibility mapping file usable by Private deployments.
implementation_steps: Write design doc and compatibility mapping spec (link to confluence)
Add conduit middleware scaffolding in runtime request pipeline (golang) and feature flag behind runtime-1.19
Implement prefix/KV reservation primitives and unit tests to ensure no kernel rebind mid-stream
Create canonicalizer component to validate and normalize tool outputs to structured-output v2
Add call-graph snapshot and signature hash generator; implement guard thresholds and fallback behaviors
Telemetry: emit events for mapping warnings, recursion hits, prefix reservations, and fallback activations
Integrate console toggles and runtime config surface (SRE + Console client)
End-to-end QA: create integration tests with streaming + multi-tool scenarios and run canary on dedicated pool
Document behavior and provide migration guide for partner tool implementers
progress_updates: 2025-02-19: Scoped design and validated kernel reconfiguration risk with infra; confirmed need for prefix reservations to avoid mid-stream kernel changes.
2025-02-21: Prototype canonicalizer for two internal tools (search, calculator); discovered legacy math tool returns 'resultText' instead of 'value' — added mapping rule.
2025-02-25: Implemented basic call-graph snapshot and deterministic signature hashing; performance microbenchmark shows 0.8ms median overhead per request on p3-like hosts.
2025-02-27: Security reviewed the provenance envelope; requested explicit opt-in for sensitive tool outputs in Private deployments (access control gating).
2025-03-01: Feature flag gated conduit merged into runtime branch behind runtime-1.19 flag; creating canary plan for next week (dedicated pool small-scale).
review_feedback: PM (Aisha Patel): Ensure fallback semantics are well-documented and that canary metrics include hallucination rate and token-cost delta.
Design (Tomás Herrera): Request example UX strings for console warning when compatibility mapping drops fields.
Security (Lina Morales): Add KMS-scoped markers for provenance envelope when tools return customer-sensitive PII; require review for default-on in Hosted.
Infra (Priya Nair): Prefer using existing KV quotas rather than introducing new reservation counters to avoid duplicate accounting complexity.
acceptance_criteria: Conduit middleware toggled via runtime-1.19 flag with no fallback errors in canary pool
All internal tool calls in streaming scenarios normalize to structured-output v2 and are marked with provenance envelope
Recursion guard triggers at configured threshold (default 3 hops) and records telemetry; documented behavior for canned fallback
Compatibility shim maps legacy keys for at least 5 documented internal tools; unmapped fields emit WARN telemetry and are visible in console
Unit and integration tests covering prefix reservation under heavy concurrent streaming load
SRE-run canary report showing <=1% median latency regression and no increase in error-rate over 72h
